title: Do not dispatch a reviewer onto a PR that is not mergeable; hold review_ready with a wait reason until the owner rebases
note_on_history: This delivery reconciles two worker generations on the same task branch. A prior worker generation (fence_generation 2, PR #5906's original push) landed a fail-open static-fact hold (task_machine.py's review_dispatch_pr_conflict_hold_reason, gated on delivery_binding.pr_merge_state -- a field no prober populates) plus a dispatch_policy.py veto and an in-memory diagnostic registry, alongside recognizing a governed `blocker` as a valid worker responsibility-transfer event. That generation's lease was reaped and this task was redispatched (replacement_generation 3, this delivery). This delivery's live GitHub mergeStateStatus check (supervisor.py + worker_runner.py) is what makes the acceptance criteria pass today, independent of any future prober. Because task_machine.py is outside this task's declared artifact contract (.orchestrator/supervisor.py, dispatch_policy.py, test_supervisor.py, worker_runner.py, test_worker_runner.py, this evidence file), the governed handoff gate correctly rejected a delivery that touched it: the prior generation's task_machine.py addition, its matching dispatch_policy.py veto, and the in-memory diagnostic registry (all fail-open dead code pending a prober that does not exist) were reverted before handoff. The prior generation's independent, in-scope fix -- recognizing a governed `blocker` as a valid RESPONSIBILITY_TRANSFER_EVENT_TYPES entry in supervisor.py -- was kept, since it is unrelated to task_machine.py and is a genuine complementary improvement.

incident.summary: Tasks were in `review` status with a bound GitHub PR that had already become mergeStateStatus=DIRTY (conflicting with dev on a shared file, bff_test_architecture_inventory.json). The supervisor's dispatch loop still emitted review_ready_dispatch and launched a reviewer worker, because dispatch admission (rewrite/dispatch_admission.py) only checks task-state/owner/reviewer/dependency facts and never re-checks the bound PR's live GitHub mergeability before dispatching. The reviewer worker then did a full review, tried to `approve`, was rejected by the canonical review-merge gate's DIRTY check (scripts/git/github_review_bridge.py ~line 783), tried `reopen`, was also rejected. The worker then exited abruptly; the supervisor's lease/heartbeat reaper classified this as worker_process_missing, triggering lost-lease recovery and redispatch.
incident.observed_impact: 345 worker_lost_lease events in 4 hours, runaway task generation counters, exhausted provider accounts, 20 post_dispatch_maintenance re-validation conflicts.

bug_reproduction.method: Unit-level reproduction in .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py: a queued review_ready_dispatch event for a task in `review` status with a current delivery_binding/review_binding, driven through supervisor.process_queue with the live PR-mergeability check mocked to report `DIRTY`.
bug_reproduction.pre_fix_behavior: Before this change, process_queue had no live GitHub check on the REASON_REVIEW_READY path: once the existing pure admission predicate (evaluate_queued_delivery_admission / rewrite/dispatch_admission.py) reported the task eligible, the loop proceeded straight to build_request/prepare_worker_workspace/start_worker_for_request and launched a reviewer worker regardless of the bound PR's live merge state -- reproducing the exact CB02/CB05/CB07 dispatch.
bug_reproduction.post_fix_behavior: The new check (supervisor.live_review_pr_merge_state + supervisor.review_pr_merge_state_is_conflicted) runs immediately after admission passes and before start_worker_for_request is reached; when it reports DIRTY, the queue event is left `pending` with a named `last_wait_reason` and start_worker_for_request is never called that cycle.

part_a_supervisor_admission.description: supervisor.process_queue now performs one live `gh pr view --repo <slug> --json number,mergeStateStatus,mergeable` check (via the same GhJsonRunner plumbing scripts/git/github_review_bridge.py already uses) for any queued REASON_REVIEW_READY event, immediately after the existing pure admission decision (evaluate_queued_delivery_admission) passes and before build_request/start_worker_for_request. If the PR reports mergeStateStatus=DIRTY, the event is left in the existing non-terminal `pending` queue state with `last_wait_reason` set to `review_pr_dirty:<owner/repo>#<pr>:<merge_state>` (reusing the same pending+last_wait_reason idiom already used for health-refresh and workspace-guard holds in the same loop) and `review_pr_dirty_hold_at` recorded. No task-state transition, no generation bump, no failure/blocker is created. Only `mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` trips the hold; UNKNOWN/BEHIND/UNSTABLE/BLOCKED (transient/other-cause signals) do not. The check fails open (returns None, no hold) on any resolution or transport failure (missing `gh` binary, unconfigured repository slug, no live PR binding), so existing MERGEABLE-PR review_ready_dispatch behavior is unchanged. A short (30s) in-process TTL cache keyed by (repository, pr) avoids shelling out to `gh` on every dispatch-loop tick for the same PR.
part_a_supervisor_admission.mechanism: New functions in .orchestrator/supervisor.py: review_bound_pr_reference, live_review_pr_merge_state, review_pr_merge_state_is_conflicted. New call site inside process_queue, right before `request = build_request(...)`.
reused_helpers: scripts/git/github_review_bridge.GhJsonRunner (same gh JSON runner the canonical review-merge gate uses)
the existing pending + last_wait_reason non-terminal-hold idiom already used elsewhere in process_queue (health_refresh_required, dirty worker worktree guard)

part_b_worker_runner_governed_exit.description: A reviewer worker's own approve/reopen attempt is rejected by the canonical review-merge gate inside the wrapped agent process, invisible to worker_runner.py. Rather than parse the child's output, worker_runner.py's existing periodic binding-recheck loop (previously used only to detect a superseded dispatch binding, see _record_dispatch_binding_revoked) now also polls the same live mergeStateStatus fact for reviewer-role workers. When it reports DIRTY, the wrapper calls the new sibling function _record_review_pr_dirty_hold (writes `review_pr_dirty_hold`, `review_pr_dirty_reason`, `review_pr_merge_state` to the worker's status file and a durable `worker_review_pr_dirty_hold` activity-log entry sharing the same `review_pr_dirty:<repo>#<pr>:<state>` wait-reason format as Part A), then stops the child the same graceful way binding revocation already does, and publishes the wrapper's terminal status as `review_pr_dirty_hold` (not `failed`). This is an explicit, named, non-terminal exit path -- never an uncaught exception or a bare abrupt exit.
part_b_worker_runner_governed_exit.supervisor_side_wiring: supervisor.update_worker_runtime_markers now propagates `review_pr_dirty_hold` / `review_pr_dirty_reason` from the worker's on-disk status file into the durable worker record (the same mechanism that already propagates runner_status/exit_code/signal). Both poll_workers' polling path and reconcile_runtime_on_boot's boot-reconciliation path now pass reason_kind="review_pr_dirty_hold" into recover_lost_worker_lease when that flag is set, and recover_lost_worker_lease treats that reason_kind exactly like an already-blocked task: the lost-lease receipt is recorded with status `held` instead of `pending`, which (per rewrite/worker_recovery.py's existing counting/consumption semantics) does not trigger reassignment/generation-bump machinery -- the same tolerance a `blocked` task already gets. This layers on top of (does not replace) the prior generation's independent fix of recognizing a governed `blocker` event as a valid responsibility transfer.
part_b_worker_runner_governed_exit.mechanism: New functions in .orchestrator/worker_runner.py: _live_review_pr_merge_state_for_task, _review_pr_merge_state_is_conflicted, _record_review_pr_dirty_hold. New check added to the existing binding-recheck branch in main()'s run loop, gated on active_role == "reviewer". Supervisor-side: update_worker_runtime_markers, the two recover_lost_worker_lease call sites in poll_workers/reconcile_runtime_on_boot, and the `held` computation inside recover_lost_worker_lease.
reused_helpers: the same GhJsonRunner plumbing as Part A (resolved relative to worker_runner.py's own checkout, not PANTHEON_STATUS_ROOT, since the command and status roots can be separate checkouts)
the existing _record_dispatch_binding_revoked governed-stop shape (explicit status fields + durable activity-log entry + graceful SIGTERM, never an uncaught exception)
the existing `held` receipt-status tolerance recover_lost_worker_lease already grants a `blocked` task

judgment_calls: Part A's wait reason is recorded on the queue-event record (`last_wait_reason`, the same field/idiom already used for health-refresh and dirty-worktree holds in process_queue), not as a task-level `waiting_for`/blocked transition -- this avoids inventing a new state file and avoids requiring a separate `unblock` transition.

Part B's supervisor-side wiring reuses the existing `held` receipt-status tolerance (already granted to a `blocked` task in recover_lost_worker_lease) rather than inventing a new receipt state, since `held` already has the exact required semantics (fenced, counted separately, no reassignment/generation bump).

worker_runner.py resolves scripts/git (for GhJsonRunner) relative to its own checkout (THIS_DIR.parent) rather than PANTHEON_STATUS_ROOT, matching how supervisor.py resolves the same tooling and correctly handling the command-root/status-root split this repository's worker architecture allows.

The prior generation's task_machine.py/dispatch_policy.py static-fact hold was reverted, not kept: it touched a file (rewrite/task_machine.py) outside this task's declared artifact contract, and the governed handoff gate correctly refused a delivery that included it. It was also fail-open dead code (no prober populates delivery_binding.pr_merge_state), so reverting it changes no observable behavior.

This delivery reconciles two worker generations on the same task branch (fence_generation 2's prior push, PR #5906, merged via rebase with this generation's commit) rather than force-overwriting the prior generation's work; the in-scope, independent parts of that generation's work (blocker-as-terminal-event recognition) were kept, and the out-of-scope/dead-code parts were reverted.
